H.answer: No, the Supreme Court in United States v. E. C. Knight Co. (1895) did not hold that the Sherman Antitrust Act gives the federal government plenary police power over local manufacturing monopolies. According to Document 2 (ID: 156_0001-01), the Court held that the monopoly and restraint denounced by the act are a monopoly in interstate and international trade or commerce, and not a monopoly in the manufacture of a necessary of life. The Court found that the acquisition of Philadelphia refineries by a New Jersey corporation, and the business of sugar refining in Pennsylvania, bear no direct relation to commerce between the States. (Document 2)
